Our very own Craig & Krista Bell were just on Twin Cities Live, giving Elizabeth Ries and Ben Leber the inside scoop on Voyagaire and Voyageurs National Park! Check it out here!
WATCH NOW
Largest Fleet of Houseboat Rentals in Minnesota
Enjoy Voyageurs National Park on a houseboat. Stay at one spot or move around throughout the park. Our houseboats are easy to drive and navigate, and we always have help within the park should you ever want it. With 34 houseboats available, we can accommodate your group, no matter how big or small.
If you are worried about driving the boat, reserve an Assistant Captain who will be at your side to guide you from the dock through the park, help set up your campsite, and head back to the lodge once you re comfortable.
Find your Houseboat
As Featured in National Geographic
We were recently featured in National Geographic s 6 alternatives to the most popular national park lodges . Voyagaire is highlighted as one of the best places to visit as an alternative to the country s most popular national parks. With so many breathtaking national parks in the country, Voyageurs is often overlooked. We would like the opportunity to offer you the gateway into one of the most beautiful locations in The United States.
Read The Article
Book Your Stay at Voyagaire Lodge
Experience the stunning beauty of Crane Lake in the comfort of Voyagaire Lodge. Nestled amongst towering pine trees and miles of pristine northern Minnesota natural shoreline, we feature 14 pet-friendly guest rooms. Our friendly staff will ensure you have an unforgettable vacation by providing our superior hospitality.
Explore the Lodge
Enjoy the Best Food on Crane Lake
Whether you eat in our dining room or our lakeside deck, you ll agree we serve the best food around! And if you are in the mood for drinks, head to the Broken Skeg Bar. The Broken Skeg features a 360° view and a selection of quality wine and spirits, including bottled beer and eight different beer choices on tap.
View Hours
Make Yourself at Home on the Water
Our houseboats have all the amenities of home plus a few extra luxuries. Some have hot tubs, others have slides, and all have access to our famous hospitality boat. If you need anything, exceptional food or beverage, give us a call on the radio. We make daily deliveries and can bring just about anything wherever you are in the park!
View Boats
Discover Our Area Attractions
At Voyagaire Lodge, you can enjoy hiking, fishing, golfing, riding hundreds of miles of ATV trails: bring your own or rent a brand-new side-by-side from us—or settle into your private getaway aboard one of our luxurious houseboats. Whatever way you decide to spend your time here, you will love it here!

Voyagaire Lodge Guest Rooms
Guests can choose from various unique room designs, with all fourteen rooms featuring impressive pinewood and tongue and groove craftsmanship throughout.
Features
Each room in the lodge features:
Private Bath
Two or Three Queen Size Beds
Satelite TV
Microwave
Mini Fridge & Coffee Maker
Other special room features:
Suite #1, on the lower level, is an ADA accessible suite with a full kitchen and wheel-in shower
Suites #13 & #14 have complete kitchens with beautiful lake views
Some rooms have private decks
ALL of them will make you feel right at home
Winter Lodging
We are open year around! Book your snowmobile adventure at the lodge you can even rent a snowmobile from us. For maps of nearby trails, visit the MN DNR website .
Winter cancellation: If you cancel due to winter weather (i.e. lack of snow), your booking with be put into a credit to be used within one year.
Room Rates
Depending on occupancy we may be able to accommodate one night stays. Please call us at (800) 882-6287 to check availability.

We Are Pet-Friendly
We welcome pets in the Lodge and on most of our houseboats. For a non-refundable charge of $20 per night, your pet can join your lodge stay. For $20 per night, pets can climb aboard your houseboat vacation!
Pet owners are responsible for cleaning up after their animals and must keep their dogs on leash while on the Lodge property. Please notify us beforehand if you plan to bring your pet along with you on vacation.
We have a gift shop on the main floor of the Lodge. While the Lodge is brand new, our beautiful location and famous Voyagaire hospitality remain the same Exceptional!
Come Hungry
Voyagaire Lodge is home to one of the best restaurants on Crane Lake. Guests who rise early with the local wildlife are welcome to enjoy a hearty breakfast before beginning their day of exploring the  area attractions.  After a day of hiking or fishing, enjoy sizzling steaks and fresh fish! Then, cap off your evening with drinks at the Broken Skeg, our bar that has a 180* view!  Dine with us!

FAQ
Here are answers to some of the more frequently asked questions for parties interested in houseboat vacations. If you still have questions or would like more information, please don t hesitate to contact us; we are happy to assist you with your plans.
NOTICE: New Boater Education Law
Starting July 1, 2026, certain adults and youth must have a valid watercraft operator’s permit to operate motorized boats or personal watercraft. The requirement begins with those born after June 30, 2000, and phases in through 2028. Youth under 12 can t operate boats over 75 horsepower, and those using lower-powered boats must be supervised. Exemptions apply for licensed maritime professionals, short-term visitors, and emergencies. Rentals are only allowed for those 18+ with a permit.  To learn more visit the DNR s website.
Do we have to start our houseboat vacation on a particular day?
No, you may start your houseboat vacation any day as long as the boat is available. A week is seven nights, and there is a three-night minimum.
Can we do 2 nights on a houseboat?
No. We have a 3 night minimum for multiple reasons. 1). It takes considerable manpower to clean, prep, and launch a houseboat; 2) Because of our depart and return times, you would only have 1 full day in the park, which is not ideal for a good experience.
When do we depart and return?
If you are lodging with us the night before your houseboat trip you qualify for priority boarding between 11:00am-1:00PM. If you are arriving the day of your trip, you may board your houseboat between 1:00PM-3:00PM . If not checked in by 4:00PM houseboats will not be allowed to depart until the following day.
Houseboats must be back to the dock by 9:00AM on your final day. This is so we can clean the houseboat to prepare for the next guests later that day.
How much fuel will we use during our houseboat trip?
We estimate 5 to 15 gallons per day on average, though usage will vary widely based on the size of the houseboat and hours spent cruising. Typically a houseboat will not need refueling in a week s time. But for those needing gas, our hospitality service may be called to refuel the houseboat and/or the small boats. Fuel is also available at a few points throughout the Park. Remember, fuel is not included in the cost of your houseboat rental . Due to increase in fuel costs, you can expect to spend $200-$500 on fuel, dependent on boat size and the amount of cruising.
What are the standard features on all houseboats?
All houseboats are equipped with hot/cold running water, full bathrooms with showers, radio/CD player, gas BBQ grill, refrigerator/stove, furnace, all cooking/eating utensils, blankets/pillows, maps, screened windows, a cooler, deck chairs, life jackets, anchor/tie-up ropes, and a 12-volt outlet.
What is the hospitality service?
We offer room service with a wake only at Voyagaire! Call the lodge on your marine radio by 10 a.m. the morning you need room service to have the daily delivery boat stop at your houseboat. Give us a list of the items you need or want, such as gas, bait, ice, pop, or food. Our delivery boat will stop by your houseboat that afternoon or early evening. You can go about your day, and our friendly drivers will catch up to you. There is a small one-time fee for this service.
Do we need to purchase a Park permit?
Yes. Voyageurs National Park requires all houseboats to have and display an overnight permit. The permits are not site-specific, just an overnight fee for being in Voyageurs National Park. For more information on these permits and photos of some houseboat sites, visit the Voyageurs National Park website. You can click here to make a reservation and print your permit. Tip: Use Google Chrome as your web browser when printing the permit, as the site isn t compatible with some other browsers, such as Internet Explorer.
Houseboat Overnight Recreation Fee: $15 per houseboat per night
Reservation Fee: There is a $10 non-refundable reservation fee per transaction
Are pets allowed?
Yes. We accept pets in the lodge and houseboats for a non-refundable charge of $20 per pet per night. Pet owners are responsible for cleaning up after their animals and must keep their dogs on a leash while at base. Please notify us beforehand if you plan to bring your pet along with you on vacation.
When is the water warm enough to swim?
The lakes are normally warmest from mid-June to Labor Day.
Do we need any special navigational skills or licenses to operate a Voyagaire Houseboat?
No. We provide a complete set of fully marked charts and an informational booklet aboard each houseboat. A chain of color-coded and numbered buoys runs from one end of Voyageurs National Park to the other, each reflected on your map in its corresponding location. Even first-time houseboaters find this system very easy to follow.
Do we need a Canadian fishing license?
To fish in Ontario, you must have an Ontario fishing license. Most of the lakes you will be cruising, and all of the Voyageurs National Park waters are within the Minnesota boundary. Some avid fishermen purchase both a Minnesota and an Ontario license.
Do we need a fishing boat?
Coast Guard rules require a fishing boat and a 9.9 hp motor with each houseboat charter. You may either bring your own or rent one from us. Multiple boats, larger boats, runabouts, bass boats, and pontoon boats are easily towed behind the houseboat with the tow bar supplied.
Are there generators?
